Verified the chain against the exact published statements before using it — cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals gives exp: R -> (0,infinity), so e = exp(1) > 0 and def-real-power's a^x := exp(x log a) applies at a = e; def-natural-logarithm gives log(exp y) = y, so log e = log(exp 1) = 1; hence e^x = exp(x log e) = exp(x). Round 4. Correct as a proof-text objection, and NOT fatal: the Statement does not overstate. I checked the Statement against the approved PLAN Table-A row and they agree -- unique theta in (0,pi/2) with (A/H,O/H)=(cos theta,sin theta); the unit-circle arc from (1,0) to (A/H,O/H) has radian measure theta; the coordinate right triangle therefore satisfies cos theta = A/H and sin theta = O/H. No interior-angle equality is asserted in the title or the Statement, so the fatal class 'a title or Statement asserting more than the proof gives' is not met. But the PROOF did assert it: step 8.1 ended 'so its acute angle at the origin is the angle of step 7.1', identifying the triangle's interior angle at the origin with the swept unit-circle angle. I searched the library for anything that could license it and found nothing: def-radian-angle-by-unit-circle-arc-length assigns radian measure only to the counterclockwise arc of gamma from (1,0) to gamma(t), there is no definition of the angle between two rays or of a triangle's interior angle anywhere in items/, and no scaling-invariance result for angles. Terra is right that P = H(cos theta, sin theta) delivers only the positive-scalar relation. Repaired by scoping back, not by inventing an angle-invariance theorem: step 8.1 now concludes that P is the positive multiple H of the unit-circle point gamma(theta) at which step 7.1's arc ends and that the triangle's leg-to-hypotenuse ratios are that point's two coordinates; step 9.1 now states exactly the Statement's three assertions; and a Remark says plainly that no interior angle of the triangle is measured or claimed here. DeepSeek passed this text and its pass is untouched by the repair only in the sense that the mathematics is unchanged -- the item's hash moved, so it rejudges.
